subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: For Codex OAuth sibling-model failover, should OpenClaw keep Codex models on the app-server and investigate the suspected upstream websocket/rate-limit context bug first, or add direct-runtime Codex Harmony tool-call support so direct OpenClaw routing becomes a supported fallback?
rationale: Both paths are plausible but affect runtime ownership, provider fallback semantics, and tool-call parsing; automation cannot safely choose the product direction without live quota evidence and maintainer intent.

options.title: Investigate app-server first
options.body: Keep the Codex app-server as the default, land the model-scoped bookkeeping repair separately, and require live proof of the suspected websocket/rate-limit context bug before changing routing.

options.title: Add direct Harmony adapter
options.body: Implement direct OpenAI/Codex Responses Harmony tool-call parsing with real tool-use proof, then consider an explicit direct-runtime fallback for Codex OAuth models.

options.title: Wait for stronger repro
options.body: Leave this issue open until a maintainer-owned live repro captures the sibling-model 429 mismatch with redacted app-server and direct-endpoint traces.

recommendation.title: Investigate app-server first
recommendation.body: Keep the Codex app-server as the default, land the model-scoped bookkeeping repair separately, and require live proof of the suspected websocket/rate-limit context bug before changing routing.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent OpenAI/Codex routing, provider identity, and catalog commits make this the closest available owner for the runtime-direction choice.
